This analysis included three regression models: • Nighttime after 10 p.m. for the after LED conversion period (8). This model was developed with negative binominal regression with random effects using nighttime crash data for C2 roadways in Cambridge and HPMS roadways for Somerville. • Nighttime after midnight for the after LED conversion period (9). This model was developed with negative binomial regression with random effects, as well using the nighttime crashes for C1 roadways in Cambridge and HPMS roadways in Somerville. 65 • Nighttime after 8:00 p.m. for the after LED conversion period (10). This model was developed using linear regression with mixed effects based on nighttime crashes on C3 roadways in Cambridge and local streets in Somerville. 4.2.1.3.1 Nighttime Crashes on Local Roadways after 8:00 P.M. This analysis used an LMM to analyze the correlations between ND crash ratios and LED lighting levels on C3 roads in Cambridge and non-HPMS roads in Somerville. The purpose was to identify potential correlations between a number of field-measured lighting levels and nighttime crashes as an indicator of whether dimmed lighting levels affect nighttime safety. The lighting measures considered in this project included average horizontal illuminance, minimum horizontal illuminance, maximum horizontal illuminance, and standard deviation of horizontal illuminance. To avoid potential collinearity effects on the model performance, separate models were developed for lighting measures as they are highly linearly correlated. However, none of the lighting measures were found significant during this analysis. 4.2.1.3.2 Nighttime Crashes on C2 Roadways after 10:00 P.M. The purpose of this analysis was to model the correlations between the field lighting measurements and the nighttime crashes after 10:00 p.m. on C2 roadways in Cambridge and non-HPMS roadways in Somerville.
